findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876 — The `OptimizedCursorPaginator` negative-offset branch does `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset` negative on a live Django `QuerySet` (returned unevaluated from `build_queryset`), which raises Django's "Negative indexing is not supported" exception rather than the comment's claimed "properly handles negative slicing automatically," so any org member with `has_global_access` (not just superusers) can trigger an unhandled 500 by sending a crafted negative cursor offset with `optimized_pagination=true`.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876 — The comment "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" is non-sequitur to the negative-offset behavior it's attached to — no permission filtering is applied to the queryset at slice time, and the actual safety of negative slicing depends entirely on incidental Django ORM exception-raising, not on any explicit boundary/permission check as implied.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The new clamp `max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` in the shared `BasePaginator.get_result` only sanitizes the forward-pagination path; a negative offset combined with `cursor.is_prev=True` is passed to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` unclamped, so the "safe...boundary conditions" comment doesn't hold for previous-page cursors on this endpoint (and any other endpoint using `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator`).

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:69 — enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` without a None check; if `member` can be `None` for a valid non-superuser authentication context (e.g. certain internal/service auth paths), this raises `AttributeError` instead of cleanly denying the advanced-pagination feature.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New `optimized_pagination` boolean param is undocumented and untyped (raw string compare to `"true"`), giving no discoverability or validation for external API consumers

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:92 — Response envelope (`{"rows": ..., "options": ...}`) is unchanged, but which paginator produced `rows`/cursor headers is now conditional and not reflected anywhere in the response body for consumers to detect

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:23 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod filtering leaves the audit log queryset completely unbounded before pagination, so every request (paginated or not) must traverse and offset-count against the full, ever-growing AuditLogEntry table instead of a bounded time window, defeating the stated "high-volume audit logs" performance goal

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:857 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result still does list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) exactly like BasePaginator, so deep pages (large cursor.offset) still require the DB to skip `offset` rows every request — an O(offset) cost that grows without bound now that the query has no date filter; the class delivers no real algorithmic improvement over the paginator it replaces

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — The "optimized" path is only reachable via a client-supplied optimized_pagination=true flag for superusers/global-access members, meaning the alleged high-volume perf fix does not apply to the normal (non-superuser) request path that most audit-log traffic will use, leaving the common case unbounded and unoptimized

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:895 — enable_advanced_features negative-offset branch (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` with start_offset negative) forces Django to materialize/slice via list() semantics that are not natively supported for querysets with negative bounds, so on large unbounded audit tables this is likely to trigger full evaluation or repeated failed queries rather than the claimed "efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning"

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:815 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator class (~95 lines) duplicates almost all of BasePaginator.get_result with no query-plan changes (no new indexes, no changed ORDER BY/WHERE strategy), adding maintenance surface and a second code path to keep in sync without measurable throughput/latency benefit

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — A forged previous-page cursor can retain a negative offset and trigger uncaught Django negative-slice errors across BasePaginator endpoints, enabling repeated remote 500 responses.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:184 — BasePaginator.get_result offset-clamping change (start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset) alters slicing behavior for every existing paginator subclass with zero regression tests exercising negative or prev-cursor offsets before/after the change

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:850 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset code path (enable_advanced_features + cursor.offset < 0) that bypasses normal pagination bounds has no unit test verifying it can't be used to read out-of-range/unauthorized rows or that it behaves correctly at dataset boundaries
src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — Cursor.offset now implicitly supports negative values per comment but no test asserts Cursor construction/serialization round-trips correctly for negative offsets

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876 — The comment "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" is non-sequitur to the negative-offset behavior it's attached to — no permission filtering is applied to the queryset at slice time, and the actual safety of negative slicing depends entirely on incidental Django ORM exception-raising, not on any explicit boundary/permission check as implied.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the negative-offset branch states "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level", but the paginator itself applies no permission logic at slice time—it simply slices whatever `queryset` it was given (`results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`). The safety of allowing negative offsets is therefore unrelated to permissions as written, making the comment misleading/non-sequitur per the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The new clamp `max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` in the shared `BasePaginator.get_result` only sanitizes the forward-pagination path; a negative offset combined with `cursor.is_prev=True` is passed to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` unclamped, so the "safe...boundary conditions" comment doesn't hold for previous-page cursors on this endpoint (and any other endpoint using `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator`).

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` (around line 182 in the diff), `start_offset` is clamped only when `not cursor.is_prev`; when `cursor.is_prev` it uses `offset` directly. Since `Cursor.offset` is now explicitly described as allowing negative offsets (`utils/cursors.py` comment) and `offset` comes from `cursor.offset`, a negative `offset` with `cursor.is_prev=True` will reach `queryset[start_offset:stop]` unclamped. Django querysets do not reliably “handle boundary conditions” for negative slicing (often raising on negative indexing), so this can break previous-page pagination and contradicts the safety comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New `optimized_pagination` boolean param is undocumented and untyped (raw string compare to `"true"`), giving no discoverability or validation for external API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new query param `optimized_pagination` in `organization_auditlogs.py` via `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`. This is a raw string comparison with no parsing/validation (e.g., other truthy values like `1`, `True` won’t work) and there’s no evidence in the diff of any typing/schema or documentation update for this new external-facing API behavior. That’s a concrete review concern but not a clear functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:92 — Response envelope (`{"rows": ..., "options": ...}`) is unchanged, but which paginator produced `rows`/cursor headers is now conditional and not reflected anywhere in the response body for consumers to detect

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes paginator selection conditional in `organization_auditlogs.py` based on `optimized_pagination` and admin access, switching between `DateTimePaginator` and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, while keeping the response body envelope unchanged (`{"rows": ..., "options": ...}`). This can create an API-compatibility/discoverability concern because pagination behavior/cursor semantics (and thus Link/cursor headers) may differ depending on that condition, but the response body does not indicate which mode was used. The diff doesn’t prove this is a functional defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue about client-facing behavior changes without explicit signaling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:23 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod filtering leaves the audit log queryset completely unbounded before pagination, so every request (paginated or not) must traverse and offset-count against the full, ever-growing AuditLogEntry table instead of a bounded time window, defeating the stated "high-volume audit logs" performance goal

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes pagination behavior (adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator` behind a query flag and tweaks slicing logic) and does not show any removal or modification of `start`/`end`/`statsPeriod` filtering on the audit log queryset. Since no time-window filtering code is present in the shown hunks, the claim that such filtering was removed and the queryset is now unbounded is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:857 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result still does list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) exactly like BasePaginator, so deep pages (large cursor.offset) still require the DB to skip `offset` rows every request — an O(offset) cost that grows without bound now that the query has no date filter; the class delivers no real algorithmic improvement over the paginator it replaces

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, results are still fetched via Django slicing `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` (including the “advanced” negative-offset branch), which relies on OFFSET/LIMIT semantics. This means large `cursor.offset` values still incur DB work proportional to the offset (deep-page penalty), so the new paginator does not provide a clear algorithmic improvement over the existing paginator behavior shown earlier in the file (`results = list(queryset[offset:stop])`). This is a concrete performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — The "optimized" path is only reachable via a client-supplied optimized_pagination=true flag for superusers/global-access members, meaning the alleged high-volume perf fix does not apply to the normal (non-superuser) request path that most audit-log traffic will use, leaving the common case unbounded and unoptimized

adjudication.rationale: In organization_auditlogs.py the new OptimizedCursorPaginator path is only taken when `request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` *and* the caller is `request.user.is_superuser` or `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. Otherwise it falls back to the existing `DateTimePaginator` path. So the change’s claimed performance improvement is opt-in and limited to a privileged subset of requests, which may undermine the stated goal for typical/high-volume audit log traffic. However, the finding’s claim that the common path is “unbounded” is not supported by the diff: the default path still paginates via `self.paginate(... paginator_cls=DateTimePaginator ...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:895 — enable_advanced_features negative-offset branch (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` with start_offset negative) forces Django to materialize/slice via list() semantics that are not natively supported for querysets with negative bounds, so on large unbounded audit tables this is likely to trigger full evaluation or repeated failed queries rather than the claimed "efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning"

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (new code), when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then performs `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices/bounds (negative start or stop typically raises an error rather than being “handled automatically”), so this branch is likely to break pagination at runtime for negative offsets rather than providing an efficient reverse-pagination path. The diff itself introduces and relies on this unsupported behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:815 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator class (~95 lines) duplicates almost all of BasePaginator.get_result with no query-plan changes (no new indexes, no changed ORDER BY/WHERE strategy), adding maintenance surface and a second code path to keep in sync without measurable throughput/latency benefit

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new ~95-line `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` that re-implements a full `get_result` flow (cursor normalization, limit clamping, queryset building, hits counting, offset/extra handling, prev logic, reversing, `build_cursor`, `post_query_filter`) instead of reusing/refactoring existing paginator logic. The only substantive behavioral delta shown is permitting negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, plus slightly different offset clamping behavior. There’s no diff-visible change to query structure (e.g., different `order_by`, filtering strategy, or index usage), so the reviewer concern about duplicated logic/added maintenance surface and a second code path to keep in sync is grounded in what’s added here, even if performance impact can’t be measured from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — A forged previous-page cursor can retain a negative offset and trigger uncaught Django negative-slice errors across BasePaginator endpoints, enabling repeated remote 500 responses.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the updated slicing logic still allows a negative start index when `cursor.is_prev` is true: `start_offset = ... else offset` followed by `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and will raise (e.g. "Negative indexing is not supported."), producing a 500 if a client forges a cursor with a negative `offset` and `is_prev=1`. The newly added `OptimizedCursorPaginator` further encourages this by explicitly allowing `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, based on an incorrect assumption that the ORM "properly handles negative slicing". This makes the reported remote-500 scenario diff-grounded and verifiable from the code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:184 — BasePaginator.get_result offset-clamping change (start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset) alters slicing behavior for every existing paginator subclass with zero regression tests exercising negative or prev-cursor offsets before/after the change

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes slicing in an existing `get_result` implementation from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = max(0, offset)` unless `cursor.is_prev` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py around the shown hunk). That is a real behavior change for any code path where `cursor.offset` can be negative and `is_prev` is false, and it will also impact any paginator subclass inheriting this `get_result` implementation. However, the claim about “zero regression tests” is not verifiable from the diff alone, so this is best classified as a diff-grounded concern about an untested/edge-case behavior change rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:850 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset code path (enable_advanced_features + cursor.offset < 0) that bypasses normal pagination bounds has no unit test verifying it can't be used to read out-of-range/unauthorized rows or that it behaves correctly at dataset boundaries

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new, nontrivial negative-offset execution path in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` that is only taken when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, and it changes slicing behavior to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset` may be negative. The PR diff does not include any accompanying tests for this new branch or its boundary behavior, so the review point about needing targeted unit coverage for this new pagination mode is diff-grounded. However, the claim about reading “unauthorized rows” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff because authorization is enforced by the queryset construction outside this snippet.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — Cursor.offset now implicitly supports negative values per comment but no test asserts Cursor construction/serialization round-trips correctly for negative offsets

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds comments in `Cursor.__init__` about allowing negative offsets; `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted negative integers before, and there are no test files shown to confirm whether round-trip tests exist or not. The finding asserts a lack of tests, which cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.
